intro: A line-by-line review of what this project claims, what it can support, and what it cannot. Every finding has a status and a next action. This page exists so a reviewer does not have to trust the site — they can check it.

findings.claim: There are 69 starred restaurants in New York (5 x 3-star, 14 x 2-star, 50 x 1-star).
findings.evidence: guide.michelin.com all-starred listing, two pages, counted row by row on 2026-11-25.
findings.caveat: The official 2025 ceremony article lists 5/15/52. See F-01.

findings.claim: There are 76 Bib Gourmand restaurants in New York.
findings.evidence: guide.michelin.com Bib Gourmand listing, two pages, counted 2026-11-25.
findings.caveat: Counted, not named row by row in this build (F-13).

findings.claim: There are 224 'Selected' (Guide-listed, no distinction) restaurants in New York.
findings.evidence: Live filter count on the Michelin site, 2026-11-25.
findings.caveat: A count only; no individual rows were tabled.

findings.claim: Nine restaurants have captured detail (address, cuisine, price band, website, phone, booking route); seven of those also have full weekly hours.
findings.evidence: MICHELIN detail pages for Eleven Madison Park, Jungsik, Le Bernardin, Per Se, Sushi Sho, Jean-Georges, Atomix, Aquavit (hours + all fields), and Aska / Atera (all fields except hours).
findings.caveat: MICHELIN is authoritative for stars, price band and hours, but is a secondary source for a restaurant's own phone and booking partner (see S-12).

findings.claim: The remaining 60 starred rows have a name, star tier, cuisine and area, and a MICHELIN link, but no hours.
findings.evidence: The roster pages supply name/tier/cuisine/location; hours require a per-restaurant page fetch.
findings.caveat: Hours require one page fetch per restaurant. 9 of 69 are done; each further row is a single fetch, so the gap is mechanical rather than blocked.

findings.claim: Five Manhattan hotels satisfy queen-or-larger bed and a private bathroom for 2027-02-15 to 02-22.
findings.evidence: Each property page's room table was opened with the exact dates; bed type, room size and bathroom wording captured per room.
findings.caveat: The Benjamin's bath wording was not captured (F-04).

findings.claim: Eurostars Wall Street is the cheapest verified queen-bed option at $848 for 7 nights.
findings.evidence: Property page, Queen Room row, displayed stay total $848, tax $149.66 shown separately.

findings.claim: Every one of the five hotels reaches every sampled Michelin cluster within 37 minutes.
findings.evidence: 25 door-to-door Google Maps transit queries, 2026-11-25 17:14-17:31 ET.
findings.caveat: One weekday-evening sample; re-run before travel (F-11).

findings.claim: Brooklyn stars are reachable in under an hour from every shortlisted hotel.
findings.evidence: Aska (Williamsburg) legs: 30-37 min from all five hotels; the fastest downtown route is the NYC Ferry, not the L train.
findings.caveat: Only Aska was used as the Brooklyn anchor; Francie, Shota and The Four Horsemen were not timed individually.

findings.claim: MoMA, Central Park, the High Line and Top of the Rock have fully verified hours and prices.
findings.evidence: moma.org/visit, centralparknyc.org/visit, thehighline.org/visit, rockefellercenter.com ticket page.
findings.caveat: The High Line's winter window (until 20:00) applies to a February trip.

findings.claim: The Statue of Liberty is open every day 09:00-16:30 and closes only on Thanksgiving and Christmas.
findings.caveat: Neither closure falls in the trip window; the ferry is a separate third-party purchase.

findings.claim: Four venues' hours or prices could not be verified from their own pages.
findings.evidence: The Met (public hours), AMNH (ticket price), NYPL (daily hours), Katz's (opening hours).
findings.caveat: Left blank on purpose rather than copied from a secondary source (F-07).

findings.claim: 2027-02-15 to 02-22 is the cheapest of the five 7-night windows tested.
findings.evidence: Booking.com searches for five consecutive windows, cheapest qualifying row captured for each.
findings.caveat: Windows were compared on displayed pre-tax totals and several carried a dated promotion (F-12).

findings.claim: Instagram handles were verified for a small subset and rejected for two restaurants.
findings.evidence: @crownshy resolves to an unrelated 4-follower account; @jungsik is a personal account.

findings.claim: No value on this site was estimated, interpolated or remembered.
findings.evidence: Every table cell is either a captured value with a link to the page it came from, or blank with an unverified chip. MICHELIN's price band is displayed as its own field and is never converted into a dollar estimate.
findings.caveat: MICHELIN and Booking.com are authoritative but secondary for a restaurant's own phone number and a hotel's own facilities; the suggestions list proposes adding a 'primary source' chip to close that gap (S-12).

sources_registry.name: MICHELIN Guide - restaurant detail pages
sources_registry.used_for: address, phone, website, booking partner, weekly hours

sources_registry.name: Booking.com - property pages
sources_registry.used_for: room-level bed, size, bathroom, rate terms

sources_registry.name: Google Maps - transit directions
sources_registry.used_for: every transit time on the site

sources_registry.name: Rockefeller Center
sources_registry.used_for: observation deck hours and ticket tiers

method_notes: Counts come from paginated listings: the all-starred page truncates at 48 rows, so page 2 was counted separately.
Booking.com room tables were read at room level; a hotel's cheapest advertised room is frequently a twin or full bed and therefore fails the queen requirement.
Transit times are the fastest itinerary Google returned at capture, not the default selected option.
Where a venue's own page omitted a value, the cell is blank. Secondary sources were deliberately not used to fill it.
